Discover Board Game Arena Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 3 Refilling the living room 4 Game End 5 Scoring Overview Players take turns selecting tiles from the living room and placing them in their bookshelves to score points. The last round occurs when a player completely fills their bookshelf. Turn On your turn, take 1-3 items from the living room. and place them in 1 column of your bookshelf, in any order you like. Items taken must form a continuous row or column and must have 1 free edge prior to selection. Refilling the living room The living room is refilled when there are 4 or fewer items. Game End The last round is triggered when any player completely fills their bookshelf. Highest score wins. If tied, the tied player sitting furthest clockwise from the starting player wins. Scoring Personal Goal Card: Each player scores 1,2,4,6,9 or 12 points for matching 1,2,3,4,5 or 6 items on their card and bookshelf Common Goal Cards: Each game is played with 2 common goal cards. Players will score points if they complete these common goals Adjacent Item Tiles: For each group of orthogonally adjacent items, players score 2,3,5 or 8 points for sets of 3,4,5 or 6+ items Game-end trigger: The first player to completely fill their bookshelf scores 1 point Board Game Arena would like to thank Cranio Creations for making it possible to have this game here. 1648 myshelfie العربية беларуская мова български език Brezhoneg Català čeština Dansk Deutsch Ελληνικά English Español Eesti keel فارسی Suomi Français Galego עברית Hrvatski Magyar Italiano Bahasa Indonesia 日本語 한국어 Lietuvių Latviešu Bahasa Malaysia Nederlands Norsk Polski Português Română Русский язык Slovenčina Slovenščina Српски Svenska ไทย Türkçe Українська мова Tiếng Việt 中文 (漢) 中文 (汉) Application loading... ... {DISPLAY_IN_OTHER_LANG} {LANG_REDIRECT_CODE} boardgamearena.com Top Help What is Board Game Arena? [Rating: 1/10] Straight forward set collection / abstract game of taking groups of tiles and slotting them into your grid in Connect 4 style to satisfy various public or secret goals.  Fine for families but there was not enough here to be engaging.

[Rating: 1/10] Novel and very cute. But it's a one-trick pony, thus have limited shelf (hah!) life.

[Rating: 2/10] I only played this game because my wife has what the kids these days might refer to as a "fairy witch cottagecore aesthetic" and she thought this game would fit into it and be fun. This is the same woman who has played Through the Ages, Terraforming Mars and Arkham Horror with me.  Needless to say it neither fits the aesthetic nor our gaming tastes. Might be a fun welcoming game for casual players or younger gamers, but I have no desire to play again.

[Rating: 3/10] This game feels like some weird mashup of Mahjong, Connect 4 and Sagrada.  The tile selection action sounds like it could be interesting, but is really confusing in practice.  There are conflicting objectives, where you get bonuses for having similar pieces together, and others where you get bonuses for rows or columns of differing objects.  This is an example where the concept was much better than the actual implementation.  The one saving grace was that the game played really fast.

[Rating: 3/10] Take & make meets Connect 4. The puzzle aspect, the shared goals, and the personal goals in My Shelfie provide enough to think about. The topic is cozy but also vapid, something that conjures up trying to make the best of isolating indoors. Bonus - incidental malice! Overall, it just reminded that I'd much rather play other games it recalls: Nibble, Richelieu, or even Circle the Wagons.

[Rating: 3/10] [b]Spatial pattern-building with almost nothing beneath the pattern.[/b] Draft tiles, drop them into columns, satisfy adjacency and personal objectives. There is mild tactical denial and some sequencing, but virtually no meaningful long-term resource tension, strategic divergence, or cascading consequence. Cheerful and functional, yet strategically anaemic.

[Rating: 3/10] Here's how I understand the theme... as a result of your toxic codependency, you invite up to 3 of your "friends" to your private library to help pick up a bunch of your random shit that has fallen on the floor, but really it's just a way for you to show off how many trophies you have. For fear of abandonment, new messes are made once it looks like everything is cleaned up, and your narcissistic personality requires that everything picked up gets put in the same column. Besides your need for therapy, nothing else makes sense.
